query: A train leaves at 3pm at 80 km/h and another at 4pm at 100 km/h from the same station on the same track; when and where does the second catch up? Show the reasoning.

preface.title: Train Catch-Up Calculation
plan: Calculate the distance traveled by the first train in one hour
Determine the closing speed between the two trains
Compute the time and location of the intercept

scene.title: Train catch-up calculation
scene.subtitle: Relative motion and kinematic problem

answer.headline: The second train catches up at 8:00 PM at a distance of 400 km from the station.
body: The first train leaves at 3:00 PM at 80 km/h, meaning that by 4:00 PM, when the second train starts its journey, it has already covered 80 km. From this point, the second train must close this 80 km gap.

Since the second train travels at 100 km/h and the first at 80 km/h, the second train gains 20 km on the first train every hour. To close the 80 km lead, it takes 80 km ÷ 20 km/h = 4 hours of travel time.
Adding these 4 hours to the second train's 4:00 PM start time results in an 8:00 PM catch-up time. At this time, the second train has traveled for 4 hours at 100 km/h, covering exactly 400 km.
caveats: Assumes both trains maintain constant speeds.
Assumes the track length is sufficient to accommodate the 400 km distance.

items.label: Calculate head start
items.detail: Train A travels for 1 hour before Train B starts at 80 km/h.

items.label: Determine relative speed
items.detail: Train B closes the distance at 100 km/h - 80 km/h = 20 km/h.

items.label: Calculate time to close gap
items.detail: 80 km gap / 20 km/h relative speed = 4 hours.

items.label: Final time and distance
items.detail: 4:00 PM + 4 hours = 8:00 PM; 4 hours × 100 km/h = 400 km.

items.label: d = v × t
items.detail: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

items.label: t = Δd / Δv
items.detail: Time to close a gap (Δd) at a speed difference (Δv).
